title.narrative: Multitranche Financing Facility (MFF) - Improving Access To Health Services For Disadvantaged Groups Investment Program - Tranche 1

description.narrative:
Tranche 1 proposed for financing under the requested periodic financing request (PFR) aims to contribute to the investment program's impact of improving the health status of Mongolians.
The investment project comprises the following outputs:
(i) urban and rural primary health care strengthened, (ii) district and aimag hospital services improved, (iii) health financing system strengthened, and (iv) capacity in procurement and financial management of relevant government entities for health strengthened.

description.narrative: Access to affordable quality primary and secondary health servicesb in Khovd and Uvs aimags (provinces), Ulaanbaatar ger (traditional tent) areas, and selected soums (aimag subdistricts) improved

45,500 persons per year from Ulaanbaatar ger areas, and selected aimags use gender sensitive and client-friendly expanded PHC services Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: To be closely monitored. Data Source: MOH and UCHD annual statistics and reports

97,500 persons per year use improved quality district hospital and aimag general services, including modern obstetrics and gynecology, and surgery departments Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: To be closely monitored. Data Source: MOH and UCHD annual statistics and reports

An integrated strategic purchasing system is initiated involving MOF, HIO, MOH and local governments based on issued regulations Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Completed. The strategic purchasing system has been established in 2021. Data Source: Ministerial orders, MOH and MOF Base year: 2019
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: District and aimag hospital services improved Indicator: A management system for autonomous hospitals is developed, agreed, and operational in at least three hospitals (2019 baseline: 0) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: MOH engaged a consulting firm for CS04: Hospital Planning and Management in December 2021. CS04 conducted a situational analysis of the status of hospital governance and management systems, operational and financial performances, risks, and challenges in providing quality healthcare services in Uvs aimag and Khan-Uul district. CS04 consultants also developed a governance design of a semi-autonomous hospital management system that was discussed at the technical working group on June 14, 2023, and with stakeholders of MOH, MOF, UB City Health Department, referral hospitals, and experts in September 2023. The CS04 consultants submitted comments on the draft amendment to the "Health Law" that was prepared by MOH. A study comparing the management capacity of referral hospitals with and without hospital boards was completed in June 2024. The final version of the recommendations focuses on stabilizing hospital governance and strengthening and improving the monitoring of referral hospital boards. The consultant team developed site-based specific recommendations for 4 referral project hospitals. It was discussed at the meeting of the Management Board of the MOH in May 2025 and the final report submitted to MOH in June 2025. Data Source: MOH and project review reports

Output: Urban and rural primary health care strengthened Indicator: Five gender and client-friendly SHCs established in selected aimags (2019 baseline: 0) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: The project will establish four SHCs. One out of the planned five SHCs in Tranche 1 has been dropped from the project because the new hospital was already built under the government budget. The CS01 developed functional plans for four SHCs. The functional plans A, B, and C levels of 5 SHCs were accepted by the MOH TWG in May 2022; the concept designs of the SHCs were approved in Dec 2022. The detailed engineering drawings (DEDs) for 4 SHCs were completed and approved by State Expertise, and the bids were advertised in April- July 2023. The BEC for civil works was established by MOH (order A/68, May 16, 2023). Package CW03: SHC in Bayan-Under of Uvurkhangai was awarded to contract and construction was completed in Dec 2024. The packages CW02 for SHC in Erdene of Dornogobi, CW04 for SHC in Tarialan of Khuvsgul, and CW05: SHC in Dashinchilen of Bulgan were already awarded to contracts in September -October 2023. Civil works started in April - May 2024 and they are ongoing. Progress ranges between 68%-77% as of June 2025. The MOH approved a list of 98 types, 848 units of medical and non-medical equipment and furniture, and a room-to-room book for 5 SHCs under package G1 in April 2023 and signed the contract with Interscience LLC on 7 September 2024. The equipment will be supplied and installed by 1 Oct 2026. Data Source: MOH yearly project progress reports

Output: Urban and rural primary health care strengthened Indicator: Four gender and client-friendly FHCs with expanded services set up and providing health services to target population in Ulaanbaatar (2019 baseline: 0) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: The UB city allocated land for construction of 4 FHCs in 14th khoroo Khan-Uul (KHUD), 19th khoroo Chingeltei (CHD), 17th khoroo Bayanzurkh (BZD), and 26th khoroo Songinokhairkhan (SHD) districts. Project consultants developed functional plans and layouts for gender- and client-friendly FHCs (approved by MOH in 2022); concept design of FHCs (approved by UCMO in 2023) and detailed engineering drawings (DEDs) (approved by CDC in 2023). The MOH established the BEC for civil works by order A/68 dated May 16, 2023. The contracts for construction of FHCs in four districts have been signed. The construction is ongoing and progress as of June 2025 ranges between 50-75%. The packages for ground source heating pump (GSHP) were advertised twice in 2024 but failed. The EA has decided to revise the threshold price and number of packages. The rebidding for the 3rd time is planned in Q4 2025. MOH approved A/129 order for equipment list and technical specifications for 80 types of items for 3 FHCs in March 2024. The MOH signed a G01 contract with Interscience LLC for supply medical equipment for SHCs and FHCs on 11 September 2024. All medical equipment was ordered and 61 out of total 80 types of item were delivered in Mongolia and commissioned by MOH Technical Committee. The remaining equipment will be delivered, installed and training conducted by 1 Oct 2026.
Data Source: MOH yearly project progress reports

Output: District and aimag hospital services improved Indicator: Feasibility of LCT in one hospital and three FHCs demonstrated, verified and reported (2019 baseline: not applicable) Achievement: N Progress/Status: MOH engaged a consultant firm CS10 in December 2021 to introduce and install advanced LCT. The consultants provided comments on the LCT of the DED for KHUD hospital and specifications of the evaluation score for the LCT part of the bidding document for package CW08 in Section 6. The Consultants also assisted the BEC in reviewing the bidding documents. The contract was awarded to China Railway First Group Co., Ltd on December 2023. CS10 consultants are also assisted in developing bidding documents for package CW01: Installation of ground-source heating pumps in three FHCs in Ulaanbaatar. The package was advertised twice in 2024 but was unsuccessful. A rebidding is planned for Q4 2025 after changes in the number of packages and estimated value. Data Source: Monitoring and verification reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2027 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: District and aimag hospital services improved Indicator: Khan Uul district hospital of Ulaanbaatar expanded to include surgery, obstetrics and gynecology, and other disciplines; and in- and outpatient departments functionally linked (2019 baseline: NA) Achievement: N Progress/Status: In May 2021, the government proposed using the detailed engineering design (DED) of the model Songinokhairkhan District Hospital (SDH) for the new Khan-Uul District hospital. Therefore, MOH hired an individual national consultant (CS16) to propose adjustments required in the SDH drawings to the land and physical infrastructure of the existing Khan-Uul hospital. The consultant prepared four options for the general hospital plan and proposed some modifications based on new standards and construction requirements enforced by the government since 2015 after the approval of the DED. In March 2022, the MOH engaged Building Technology LLC (CS18), the author of the DED of Songinokhairkhan District Hospital, to update the DED for Khan-Uul Hospital. State experts approved the DED for Khan-Uul District General Hospital in December 2022. In October 2022, the State Procurement Agency (SPA) established the bid evaluation committee. The package CW08- KHUD hospital construction with equipment installation, including advanced LCT, was advertised on 18 January 2023. ADB approved the technical and financial-combined BER (CBER) in August 2023. MOH signed a contract with the China Railway First Group Co., Ltd on 20 December 2023. The construction started in May 2024. Progress is 34.4% as of October 2025. MOH engaged the Ulaanbaatar City Investment Department to supervise the client's construction of the Khan-Uul District Hospital. Data Source: Project report, MOH (yearly) Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2027 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: District and aimag hospital services improved Indicator: Uvs aimag hospital expanded with a new outpatient department (2019 baseline: not applicable) Achievement: N Progress/Status: Firm CS04 engaged by MOH in 2022 has developed reports on situational analysis and a patient satisfaction survey at Uvs aimag Hospital, which were accepted by MOH in June 2022. MOH accepted a functional flow plan for the extension of UVs AGH on June 30, 2022. The concept design drawings for the extension of UVs AGH were approved by Aimag General Architecture on November 09, 2022. State experts approved the DED for the new extension on April 11, 2023. The BEC for package CW10 was established in the SPA on April 26, 2023. Bid for package CW10: Construction of Extension Building of Uvs Aimag General Hospital was advertised on June 02, 2023. MOH signed a contract with JV City Landmark LLC and Happy Building LLC (Mongolia) on 25 October 2023. Construction started in April 2024. The current progress is 97% as of October 2025. MOH engaged the Construction Development Center, a state-owned enterprise, for the employer's supervision for Uvs Hospital on 28 September 2023. EA/PIU developed a list of equipment and technical specifications of 67 types and 416 units of essential non-medical and medical equipment for Uvs aimag hospital and the MOH TWG on Medical Equipment and Communication Technology approved it in Q4 2023. The procurement of package G24 with three lots started on 7 Feb 2025 and the contracts were signed on 9 July 2025. The suppliers will deliver the medical equipment by 8 Oct 2025. Data Source: Project report, MOH (yearly) Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2027 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Health financing system strengthened Indicator: 20% of HIO staff report improved purchasing capacity, including planning and negotiations skills, contracting and contract management, costing, monitoring and reporting, service quality auditing and fund management (2019 baseline: 0) Achievement: N Progress/Status: The project trained 18 master trainers in 2021. Mater trainers trained 68% of MOH staff in Module 1: Strategic Purchasing System in December 2021 and Module 2: Hospital Autonomy & Gender-sensitive Budgeting in April 2022. The project conducted 7 capacity-building training for the HIGO staff in March 2022 with the participation of 163 staff (80.9% of them were female) on new legal reforms on single buyer purchasing, strategic financing, selection of healthcare organizations, contracting, service quality, claim control, claim criteria, health services packages, reimbursement method of DRGs, calculation budget, medical auditing, requirements, selection and contracting of medical auditor, and quality assessment on medical services. The project also trained staff from 20 aimags' and remote districts' health insurance departments in modules 1 and module 2 and on the updated HIGO resolutions #1 and #5, regulation on out-pocket payments, procedures on the selection and contracting of the healthcare organization, and performance indicators for the contract. 2300 people participated in the above training (77.8% were women). In January 2024, the MOH engaged five individual consultants for health finance, costing, healthcare package, and healthcare quality. The consultants developed two technical reports: “International Experience in Introducing Health Technology Assessment and Steps to Implement It in Mongolia” and “Assessment Report on the Current Situation of the Health Benefits Package.” The project also trained total of 4,118 medical staff (76.7% women) on health financing reform, strategic purchasing, and strengthening the semi-autonomy of hospitals in 2021- 2022. These participants were from FHCs, SHCs, RDTCs, AGHs, rural general hospital, central and specialized hospitals, university hospital, district health centers and hospitals, maternity hospitals in UB city. On 6 June 2025, the MOH organized a discussion on health sector financing and hospital financial management. During the session, the Health system and Costing and payment mechanism consultants delivered two presentations titled “International trends in health financing” and ”Assessment of the budget and financial status of state-owned health organizations”, respectively. Data Source: Surveys administered to training participants Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Y Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Y Target year: 2024 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Health financing system strengthened Indicator: A strategic purchasing system is designed, and the accompanying road map and regulations issued (2019 baseline: NA) Achievement: N Progress/Status: The Strategic purchasing model in healthcare financing was approved by the Government of Mongolia in 2020 and implementation started in 2021. The project team in collaboration with consultants engaged under TA 9701-MON: Improving Health Sector Financing for Universal Health Coverage conducted a number of capacity-building activities for the Health Insurance General Office (HIGO), MOH, and public hospitals. Under the project, the project consultants developed several official documents and reports, which were subsequently adopted by the National Council on Health Insurance (NCHI) and the MOH. Data Source: Ministerial orders, MOH and MOF reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2024 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Health financing system strengthened Indicator: Sex-disaggregated data collection system established for health financing model (2019 baseline: NA). Achievement: N Progress/Status: The government has established a sex-disaggregated health insurance data collection system since 2020. Data Source: Reports and Health Insurance Organization (HIO) Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2024 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Procurement and financial management capacity of government health entities strengthened Indicator: 60% of relevant MOH and GPA staff trained on procurement, financial and risk management) for health Progress/Status: 85% (92 out of 108) of relevant staff and BEC members of MOH, SPA/GPA, Investment Department of UCMO, and (69.6% women), including the top managers were trained on ADB-financed Procurement policy and guidelines; Procurement of Works and Goods, Consultant Service Recruitment and Open competitive bidding and bid evaluation in 2022-2023. Data Source: Project report, MOH (yearly) Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2024 Target value: 60

Output: Procurement and financial management capacity of government health entities strengthened Indicator: A competency-based capacity building program developed Progress/Status: The MOH engaged procurement consultants CS23:International and CS24: National in 2022. The national consultant developed capacity-building program and training materials for relevant staff of the MOH and GPA based on training needs assessments in Oct 2022 and approved by MOH in Nov 2022. Data Source: Project report, MOH (yearly) Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2024 Target value: Y

Output: Urban and rural primary health care strengthened Indicator: An integrated primary and secondary care model piloted (2019 baseline: not applicable) Achievement: N Progress/Status: MOH engaged a consulting firm CS01 for PHC development in Dec 2021. Consultants reviewed international experience and proposed a “Hub and spoke” (GER) model for horizontal functional and vertical integration of clinical services in managing four types of diseases (hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and tuberculosis) between FHCs and district health centers (discussed by MOH TWG in June and December 2022). The model was piloted in Khan-uul and Chingeltei districts. UBHD established District Coordinating Committees (order A/140 Sep 2023) that will oversee the piloting, which started in October 2023. Consultants prepared the pilot plan, criteria for assessing the performance of FHCs in managing the four diseases, and tools for clinical audit. The PIU organized clinical training in October-November 2023, enrolling 104 physicians from 32 FHCs. The firm submitted all 15 reports (13 technical and 2 training reports) submitted. Data Source: MOH yearly project progress reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2025 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Urban and rural primary health care strengthened Indicator: LCT installed in one FHC (2019 baseline: not applicable) Achievement: N Progress/Status: MOH engaged a consulting firm for package CS10: Low Carbon Technology under the JFJCM grant in Dec 2021. The geological survey has been conducted on each FHC site. The package for 3 FHCs to install ground source heating pumps (GSHP) was procured twice but failed in 2024. In April 2025, MOH proposed to decrease the number of GSHPs from 3 to 2 and increase the bid price. The rebidding is planned in Q4 2025. Data Source: Monitoring and verification reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2025 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Urban and rural primary health care strengthened Indicator: National emergency care system established in Ulaanbaatar and aimags (2019 baseline: not applicable) Achievement: N Progress/Status: The MOH engaged a consulting firm for package CS02: Establishment of EMS on 16 June 2023. The consultant submitted inception report in July 2023. A situational analysis was conducted during August 07-18, 2023, and a functional plan for NECC based on the infrastructure assessment has been developed and discussed within MOH and UB Emergency Center in September 2023. The Detailed Engineering Design (DED) for NECC has been developed and approved by CDC in 2024. The MOH initiated the procurement of package CW07 for the construction of NECC. The first bidding failed and MOH called for the second time in September 2025. Data Source: National emergency care center yearly reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2025 Target value: Y Actual value: N
